queries.description: A declaration of all queries provided by the service.

Policy.description:
A policy document.

Defines a policy that either explicity allows or specifically denys permissions to perform one or more actions on one or more resources.

action.description: Filters which actions the policy applies to.

condition.description: The conditional modifiers that affect when the policy applies.

description.description: A long human readable description of the policy.

effect.description: The effect of the policy (i.e. allow or deny)

resource.description: Filters which resources the policy applies to.

subject.description: Filters which subjects the policy applies to.

Relationship.description:
Defines a relationship between two entities.

In GraphQL, this would represent an egde connection between two GraphQL nodes.

cardinality.description: The cardinality of the relation expressed in terms of left-to-right

denormalize.description:
Flag to indicate that the relationship is embedded in the entity.

If using "byId", then the relationship is denormalized by using the related entity identifiers. So an array of ids for a "to-many" relationship, or an identifier for a "to-one" relationship.

If using "embed", then the relationhisp is denormalized by embedding the entity schema into the left schema. So an array of objects for a "to-many" relationship, or an object for a "to-one" relationship.

description.description: A long text description of the relationship.

left.description:
The left node in the relationship.

In composition relationships, this represents the parent entity.

name.description:
The name of the relationship.

This is auto-generated if not defined.  The auto-generated name depends on the cardinality.  If the cardinality to "to-many" then the relation name is the pluralized form of the right entity, otherwise it is simply the right entity.

right.description:
The right node in the relationship.

In composition relationships, this represents the child entity.

summary.description:
A summarization of the relationship name.

For example, a physician "practices at" a facility.

type.description: The relationship type, e.g. composition vs aggregation vs association.

via.description:
This is used to indicate that the relationship is a transitive relation ship based on an intermediate relationship or sets of relationships.

For example, a region has a collection of territories, a territory has a collection of physicians, therefore a region can have a collection of physicians by applying a flatMap on all child territory physicians.  This is mostly to provide context in the diagrams.

SubjectCondition.description: A condition based on the subject attempting to perform the action on the given resource.

hasRole.description:
Adds a condition that requires the the subject has a role or one of a given set of roles.

This is the primary condition used for Role-Based-Access control.  This is useful when the collection of role names are known at design time (i.e. the roles are system defined not user defined.)

id.description: Adds a condition that matches the current subject's identifier.

SubjectIdCondition.description: Creates a condition based on the subject's identifier.

in.description: Creates a condition to check if the subject's identifier is "in" a specific collection.

Must contain at least on selection, if specified.
